findings.title: Potential SQL Injection via Unparameterized Query
findings.description: SQL statement constructed via string concatenation with request parameters. Unparameterized queries allow attackers to alter database logic.
findings.evidence: string query = "SELECT * FROM Payments WHERE AccountId = '" + request.AccountId + "' AND Amount = " + request.Amount;
findings.remediationGuidance: Use parameterized SQL queries or ORM abstractions (e.g. Entity Framework Core parameters, SqlCommand.Parameters).

findings.title: OS Command Injection via Shell Invocation
findings.description: Direct shell execution with string interpolation or concatenation detected. Untrusted arguments passed to shell interpreters enable arbitrary command execution.
findings.remediationGuidance: Avoid invoking system shells directly; use ProcessStartInfo with strongly-typed arguments and strict whitelist validation.

findings.title: Use of Broken Cryptographic Algorithm (DES/MD5)
findings.description: Deprecated cryptographic algorithm detected. DES and MD5 are vulnerable to collision and brute-force attacks and must not be used for encryption or hashing.
findings.remediationGuidance: Migrate cryptography to AES-256 (AES-GCM) for symmetric encryption and SHA-256/SHA-512 for cryptographic hashing.

findings.title: Hardcoded API Secret or Private Key
findings.description: Hardcoded sensitive secret or API key identified in configuration or source code. Secrets must be extracted into secure environment variables or secret vaults.
findings.remediationGuidance: Extract hardcoded credentials into environment variables or a secure key vault (e.g. Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager).
